  "extract_plan": {
    "chunk_summary": "Manski's conclusion: federal statistical agencies pay only lip service to the NRC's Practice 4 on openness about data limitations, do not quantify sampling/nonsampling error, and do not justify trend extrapolation, imputation, or X-12 seasonal adjustment; the paper proposes measuring transitory and permanent statistical uncertainty and urges research on how communicating uncertainty affects decision making; followed by the reference list."
  },

      "location": "5. Conclusion"
    },
    {
      "id": "c-transitory-statistical-uncertainty",
      "name": "transitory statistical uncertainty",
      "aliases": [],
      "description": "Uncertainty in estimates of official statistics that arises from their being based on incomplete data, and that resolves as data become complete.",
      "anchor": "the transitory statistical uncertainty",
      "location": "5. Conclusion"
    },
    {
      "id": "c-permanent-statistical-uncertainty",
      "name": "permanent statistical uncertainty",
      "aliases": [],
